help_info_string:
`[\]` is a bot written by Info Teddy and Dav999 in Python utilizing `discord.py`, for use on the tOLP Discord server, and TNTGB.
To get accepted into the developer team, you have to be accepted by eighty-percent of the current members of the team.
Special thanks to Shiny for making the current icon for the bot.
The bot is normally hosted by Info Teddy, but currently it is temporarily hosted on one of Dav999’s computers.

t.tntgb_only: This command can only be used on the TNTGB server.

t.rolecachedisabled: The role cache is disabled on this server.
t.generic_error:
A fault did occur.
Kindly inform any bot-programming human what you did want to occur if this fault didn’t obstruct this bot’s normal functions.
If a function of yours _is_ to program this bot, kindly ask this bot’s host for any logs from this fault.

commands.name: help
commands.short: Lists commands and their descriptions.
commands.extra: If an argument is given, `\help` will look up in-depth description of the argument.

commands.name: source
commands.short: Gives the link to the bot’s source code.

commands.name: echo
commands.short: Echoes your input.

commands.name: info
commands.short: Gives information about a user.
commands.extra: Remind Info Teddy to do more than just permissions for the user.

commands.name: findu
commands.short: Find a user by all or part of the nickname or username case-insensitively, or the discriminator, or mention, or ID.
commands.extrafull: Find a user by all or part of the nickname or username case-insensitively, or the discriminator, or mention, or ID. Displays various information about the matched user. If no argument is given, will match caller instead.

commands.name: findc
commands.short: Find a channel by all or part of the name case-insensitively, or mention, or ID.
commands.extrafull: Find a channel by all or part of the name case-insensitively, or mention, or ID. Displays various information about the matched channel. If no argument is given, will give a list of channels instead.

commands.name: hangman
commands.short: Initiate a game of Hangman. Send via private message with a custom word. Use `\stophangman` to stop.
commands.extra: Ported from DavBot.

commands.name: stophangman
commands.short: Stop the current game of hangman.
commands.extra: Can only be done by the one who started the game or a moderator.

commands.name: invite
commands.short: Links to servers \[\\\] can be used on.
commands.extra: The master instance of \[\\\] can only be used on those servers.

commands.name: countpins
commands.short: Count the amount of pins in a channel.
commands.extra: If no channel mention is given, will use the current channel instead.

commands.name: countallpins
commands.short: Count the amount of pins in all channels.

commands.name: math
commands.short: Does real math with no arbitrary precision.
commands.extra: **Syntax**: `\math <number> <operand> <number>`

commands.name: testroleconditional
commands.short: Gives the result of a given expression.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\testroleconditional <targetmember> <expression>`
For more information about the expression system, please ask Dav or read the code, a documentation will come in the future. The system is also unfinished.

commands.name: addcustomrolecommand
commands.short: Add a custom command that can give or take roles in given conditions.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\addcustomrolecommand <name> <self|input> <no|command|input|RELATIVETIME> <condition> <giveroles> <takeroles>`

For a detailed explanation, see the [wiki page](https://gitgud.io/infoteddy/bracketed_backslash/wikis/custom-commands).

Example: `\addcustomrolecommand roleban input input c.mod&~t.mod [98765] []`

commands.name: addcustomaliascommand
commands.short: Add a custom command that is an alias for another custom command.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\addcustomaliascommand <name> <aliasof>`

`name`: The name of the command you are making now
`aliasof`: The name of the command you want to run

commands.name: removecustomcommand
commands.short: Remove a custom command
commands.extra: **Syntax**: `\removecustomcommand <name>`

commands.name: archive
commands.short: Create a chat log of the latest messages in a given channel. Not available for non-admins (yet).
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\archive <channel> [limit=100]`

The maximum limit is determined by the `maxarchive` config setting, which is global for the bot.

commands.name: starboard
commands.short: Manages the starboard.
commands.extra:
You can use the following options:
`\starboard init <CHANNEL>` – Initialize the starboard settings (but suspend it first).
`\starboard set <KEY> [VALUE]` – Change a starboard config option. VALUE is needed for all options except `star` and `nostar`. See the output of `\starboard init` or the wiki for more details on the settings that can be changed.
`\starboard summarize_config` – Summarize the configuration of all the starboard settings on the server in a paragraph of English text.
`\starboard suspend` – Suspend the starboard, effectively freezing it.
`\starboard unsuspend` – Unsuspend the starboard.
`\starboard ignore <CHANNEL>` – Make messages sent in CHANNEL not eligible for being posted on the starboard.
`\starboard unignore <CHANNEL>` – Lift an ignore on a channel.
`\starboard ban <MEMBER>` – Ban a member from interacting with the starboard.
`\starboard unban <MEMBER>` – Lift a starboard ban on a member.
`\scan_danny <CHANNEL> <USERID>` – Scan the last 200 messages in a channel for messages by a previous starboard bot, so that those messages can be ignored for a smooth transition. See the wiki for more details.

commands.name: botok
commands.short: Pings the bot.

commands.name: version
commands.short: Gives the bot version and versions of libraries.

commands.name: uptime
commands.short: Gives the bot uptime and host uptime.

commands.name: restart
commands.short: Restarts the bot.

commands.name: kill
commands.short: Kills the bot.

commands.name: config
commands.short: Manages configurable settings in the bot.
commands.extra:
You can use the following options:
`\config list` – Show all the settings and their values.
`\config reload` – Reloads the configuration file.
`\config get <KEY>` – Show extended information about a specific setting and how it is configured, given its key.
`\config set <KEY> <VALUE>` – Update the value of a given non-array setting.
`\config insert <KEY> [INDICE] <VALUE>` – Insert a value into an array or dic setting. `[INDICE]` is required for dics.
`\config remove <KEY> <VALUE/INDICE>` – Remove a value from an array or dic setting.
`\config detach <KEY>` – Make this setting no longer use the master value, and use a server-specific value instead.
`\config reattach <KEY>` – Make this setting use the master value.
`\config default <KEY>` – Sets the setting back to default.

commands.name: gamestatus
commands.short: Sets the game status

commands.name: eval
commands.short: Evaluates your argument as code.

commands.name: evalawait
commands.short: Evaluates your argument as code and precedes it with `await`.

commands.name: evalawaitfile
commands.short: Evaluates `eval.txt` as code and precedes it with `await`.

commands.name: setvar
commands.short: Sets a global variable.
commands.extra: **Syntax**: `\setvar <VARIABLE> <ASSIGNMENT>

commands.name: reloadstrings
commands.short: Reloads strings.

commands.name: uploadfile
commands.short: Uploads a file from the current working directory of the bot.
commands.extra: Made so Dav999 could stop asking me to upload so much files. Also, try not to upload a file that’s too large, it’ll basically slow down the entire bot.

commands.name: kick
commands.short: Kicks a member from the server.

commands.name: serverban
commands.short: Bans a member from the server.

commands.name: unserverban
commands.short: Unbans a user from the server.

commands.name: bans
commands.short: List all server bans on this server.

commands.name: move
commands.short: Redirect the current conversation to a different channel by sending messages in both channels and linking between them.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\move <CHANNEL> [SUBJECT]`

	`<CHANNEL>`: You can supply a channel (mention, (part of) name, id, etc) to move the conversation to.

	`[SUBJECT]`: Optionally, you can also supply the subject of the conversation, so the messages will include something like "the conversation about _code indentation styles_".

commands.name: voicemute
commands.short: Mutes a member in a voice channel.

commands.name: voiceunmute
commands.short: Unmutes a member in a voice channel.

commands.name: votevoicemute
commands.short: Starts a vote on whether to mute a member in a voice channel.

commands.name: vy
commands.short: Votes yes in a voice mute vote.

commands.name: vn
commands.short: Votes no in a voice mute vote.

commands.name: vc
commands.short: Cancels a voice mute vote.

commands.name: rolerst
commands.short: Resets the roles for a member back to the normal state.
commands.extra: Removes all restrictive roles from a user, and gives back the `tOLPer` role if necessary if run again.

commands.name: rolecacherst
commands.short: Removes a member’s roles from the role cache.
commands.extra: Only accepts a user ID.

commands.name: expires
commands.short: Sets an expiry time for a member’s restrictive role. It will carry out a role reset after the specified time has elapsed.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\expires <TIME> [MEMBER]`

	`<TIME>`: A relative time in the format `[#d][#h][#m][#s]`. The units have to be in the correct order.
	**Examples**: `7d12h`, `1h`, `1d`, `1d2h3m4s`, `1d20s`.

	`[MEMBER]`: The member to set the expiry time for. Matches by part of the nickname or username, or all of the discriminator, ID, or mention.
	If not given, the latest member to have been given a restrictive role will instead be chosen.

commands.name: expiryremove
commands.short: Cancels the expiry timer for a member’s restrictive roles.
commands.extra: Accepts a member representation.

commands.name: expirylist
commands.short: Gives a list of all expiry timers that are currently running.
commands.extra: If run inside a direct message, it will take a server as an argument (which can be its ID, or part or all of its name), and will give an expiry list of that server if you are actually on that server.

commands.name: rolecacheadd
commands.short: Gives a user a role in the role cache.
commands.extra: **Syntax**: `\rolecacheadd <ID> <ROLE ID>

commands.name: rolesync
commands.short: Resyncs the roles cache with the current roles every member has. Does not remove roles from members who have left the server.

commands.name: rolecacheinfo
commands.short: Shows the roles that are stored in the role cache for a specific user.
commands.extra: Only accepts a user ID.

commands.name: getrawmessagecontent
commands.short: Gets the raw content of a message and its embeds.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\getrawmessagecontent [CHANNEL] <MESSAGE ID>`

	`[CHANNEL]`: A channel mention.
	`<MESSAGE ID>`: The ID of the message.

commands.name: blacklist
commands.short: Blacklists a person from using the bot server-wide.
commands.extra: Yes, you can blacklist yourself. If you do that, you deserve it and everyone will laugh at you for doing so.

commands.name: blackunlist
commands.short: Blackunlists a person, allowing one to use the bot once again.

cmds.cat_desc: Commands to manage the behind-the-scenes of the server.

commands.name: joinchannel
commands.short: Manages the join channel for the server.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\joinchannel <set|unset|get> [CHANNEL]`

	`set`: Sets the join channel.
	`unset`: Unsets the join channel.
	`get`: Gives the current join channel.
	`[CHANNEL]`: A channel mention. Required when using `set`.

commands.name: channelperms
commands.short: Gives an overview of permissions for all channels for all groups or a specific member.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\channelperms [MEMBER]`

	`[MEMBER]`: The member for which to calculate permissions. If left out, give a table for all overwrites.

commands.name: rules
commands.short: View the server’s rules.
commands.extra: **Syntax**: `\rule [RULE NUMBER]`

commands.name: rulefind
commands.short: Find rules that contain a given search term.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\rulefind <TERM>`
**Example**: `\rulefind spam`

commands.name: ruleadd
commands.short: Insert a given `<STRING>` to `[POSITION]`. If no position is given, it’s appended at the end.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\ruleadd [POSITION] <STRING>`
**Examples**:
	`\ruleadd No trolling` – Inserting a string with no position. This will be appended at the end.
	`\ruleadd 1 The most important rule is not to follow this rule.` – Inserting a string, and making it rule 1.

commands.name: ruleedit
commands.short: Edit a given rule.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\ruleedit <RULE NUMBER> <STRING>`
**Example**: `\ruleedit 2 No trolling`

commands.name: rulemove
commands.short: Move a given rule to a different position, with nothing overwritten.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\rulemove <RULE NUMBER> <NEW POSITION>`
**Example**: `\rulemove 2 4`

commands.name: ruleremove
commands.short: Remove a given rule.
commands.extra:
**Syntax**: `\ruleremove <RULE NUMBER>`
**Example**: `\ruleremove 2`

commands.name: rulemaint
commands.short: Toggle normal members being able to see the rules for this server.

commands.name: selfban
commands.short: Bans the caller on TNTGB without needing a moderator to do it.
commands.extra: Use this command in the channel the mistake was made in.

commands.name: b
commands.short: Rolebans a member on TNTGB.
commands.extra:
Use this command in the channel the mistake was made in. Takes a member representation (full or part of their name, or their discriminator, ID, whatever you want) as the first argument, and a reason as the second argument.
If you input a member name with spaces, you can separate the two arguments with a newline.
**Examples:** ```\b testuser using spaces
``````
\b some member
writing "the"```

commands.name: b_id
commands.short: Rolebans a member on TNTGB, given an ID. This can also ban members who have left the server.
commands.extra: Same as `\b`, except it only accepts an ID.

commands.name: b_mod
commands.short: Same as `\b`, but allows lifting the oldest two bans by banning a moderator.
commands.extra: That’s basically the only difference, it lifts the protection on banning mods (because unbanning two members can’t be undone as simply)

commands.name: revertban
commands.short: Reverts a ban on TNTGB.
commands.extra: Removes the original ban log entry as well! Takes a member representation.

commands.name: tntgb_maint
commands.short: An admin toolbox of maintenance features specifically for TNTGB.
commands.extra:
Assumes you know what you’re doing. Can only be used by an administrator.
**Options:**
`\tntgb_maint liftmsg` – Edit a message in the ban log channel to change the "⛔" into "[LIFTED]", but don’t announce it. Takes message ID.
`\tntgb_maint addtimer` – Adds an expiry timer for the first user mentioned in the message based on the timestamp of the message. If sent by the bot, it’ll also automatically edit the message when the timer expires.
